evals.prompt: I want to add rate limiting to the /api/auth/login endpoint in this repo. The Confirmed Intent is: Outcome: prevent brute-force on login; User: all users; Why now: security audit flagged it; Success: 5 failed attempts per IP per 15 min triggers a 429; Constraint: must not require Redis (use in-memory or existing Postgres); Out of scope: account lockout. Produce a spec-and-plan artifact.
evals.expected_output: TRIGGER — behavioral. Skill should produce a markdown file at docs/plans/rate-limiting.md containing: (a) six-area spec with stable R-IDs covering the 429 threshold requirement, the no-Redis constraint, and the out-of-scope boundary for account lockout; (b) implementation units as ### U1, ### U2, etc. headings with no checkbox lists; (c) each unit contains Goal, Requirements citing R-IDs, Dependencies, Files as repo-relative paths under src/, Approach in plain prose decisions, Test scenarios enumerating happy-path (5 failed attempts trigger 429), edge cases (4 attempts, 6 attempts, IP rotation, 15-min window reset), error paths (Postgres unavailable, counter read failure), and integration scenarios (middleware stack, Postgres persistence across requests); (d) Status line stamped 'READY — reviewed <date>; verdict READY' after up-the-hill review completed within 5 rounds.
expectations: The skill fires (TRIGGER)
Output contains ### U1 and ### U2 headings (no checkbox items)
Every unit cites at least one R-ID in its Requirements field
R-ID for the no-Redis constraint appears in at least one unit or is deferred in Scope Boundaries
Test scenarios for each unit enumerate input, action, and expected outcome
Happy-path scenario names '5 failed attempts' and '429' response
No implementation code blocks (no method signatures, no SQL DDL) appear in any unit Approach section
Status line reads 'READY' after up-the-hill review

evals.prompt: Spec and plan a migration of the user table from integer IDs to UUIDs. No Confirmed Intent doc exists — infer from the request. This is a data migration touching auth, sessions, and foreign keys.
evals.expected_output: TRIGGER — behavioral. Skill should produce a markdown file at docs/plans/uuid-migration.md containing: (a) six-area spec with R-IDs including boundary entries for rollback strategy and FK cascade behavior; (b) depth classified as Deep because the migration touches external contract surfaces (session cookies encoding user IDs, API responses returning user IDs, FK constraints across multiple tables); (c) implementation units with U-ID headings (### U1 through at least ### U4) covering schema change, FK migration across sessions and related tables, session handling and token invalidation, and verification/rollback procedure — each unit citing R-IDs and listing repo-relative file paths under db/ and app/models/; (d) test scenarios per unit including integration scenarios proving FK consistency across users, sessions, and related tables that unit-level mocks cannot verify; (e) tangential cleanups such as index optimization routed to a Deferred subsection in Scope Boundaries rather than active units; (f) Status stamped 'READY — reviewed <date>; verdict READY' after up-the-hill review loop; (g) no implementation code (no Ruby method bodies, no SQL DDL blocks) in the plan body.
expectations: The skill fires (TRIGGER)
Depth is classified as Deep (not Standard or Lightweight)
Output contains at least ### U1 through ### U4 headings
Every unit cites at least one R-ID in its Requirements field
Integration test scenarios appear for FK consistency across users, sessions, and related tables
Tangential cleanups (e.g., index optimization) are in a Deferred subsection in Scope Boundaries, not active units
No Ruby method bodies or SQL DDL blocks appear in any unit Approach section
Status line reads 'READY' after up-the-hill review
